note: Teaching text, clarifying questions, inferred constraints and own examples. Inferred, not official. Examples are small generated inputs with outputs from the independent references in oracles.py.

clarifyingQuestions: Is a leading plus sign or zero padding ever expected?
How should -2**31 be handled in a 32-bit language?
hints: Handle zero separately or make the digit loop run at least once.
Work on the magnitude and remember the sign.
Collect digits least significant first with value % 10, then reverse.
invariants: digits collected so far are the low-order digits of the magnitude
no leading zeros except for the value 0
chooseWhen: A built-in conversion is unavailable or disallowed
tradeoffs: Working on a negative accumulator avoids overflow in 32-bit languages; Python and JavaScript have no overflow so the magnitude is safe here

constraints: 1 <= len(tokenAlphabet) <= 5000, distinct entries of 1..30 lowercase letters
single-character prefix covers every text character
clarifyingQuestions: When a token has several splits into earlier tokens, do all of them merge?
Is each token applied once, in alphabet order, or repeatedly until no change?
Do overlapping matches resolve left to right?
hints: Every id in the sequence when token j is processed is smaller than j.
A pair can only merge into j if its two strings concatenate to token j, so enumerate the splits of token j.
Index adjacent pairs by (left id, right id) and merge candidate positions in sequence order, skipping stale entries.
invariants: the linked list always spells text
the pair index contains every live adjacent pair (possibly with stale extras)
chooseWhen: Many tokens and a long text, where rescanning per token is too slow
tradeoffs: The pair index uses memory proportional to the number of merges; a plain rescan is simpler for short inputs
hack2hire:69e2411e95e80ae213e5d633.variantLabel: Inferred: merge-pass tokenizer over an ordered token alphabet

clarifyingQuestions: With cycle on, does each array wrap independently or does the whole sequence restart?
What should next() do when nothing remains?
Are empty arrays allowed?
hints: Only arrays that still have elements take part in a round.
A FIFO of cursors gives round-robin order for free.
When cycling, rebuild the cursor queue from the original arrays as soon as it empties.
invariants: the queue holds one cursor per array with remaining elements, in round-robin order
cursors never move past the end of their array
chooseWhen: Arrays have very different lengths and values are consumed lazily
tradeoffs: Materialising the sequence is simpler but costs memory for the whole pass
hack2hire:678d6982fa7ce9616e190fb3.variantLabel: Inferred: round-robin iterator with optional restart

clarifyingQuestions: Must the route end exactly at the last index?
Is the starting value counted?
What are the real limits on n?
hints: The best score at an index depends only on the best scores at the indices that can jump to it.
Those indices are i-1 and i-p for primes p ending in 3.
Precompute those primes with a sieve and take the maximum over the few predecessors.
invariants: dp[i] is the best score of any route from 0 that ends at i
chooseWhen: n is moderate and the stride set is sparse
tradeoffs: The prime stride set rules out the deque trick of the referenced problem; cost grows with the number of primes
hack2hire:69e931b2fbaf3da641828684.variantLabel: Inferred: max-score jump game with prime-3 strides

clarifyingQuestions: Is the output indexed by prefix length starting at k?
Can values repeat?
hints: Only the k largest values seen so far can ever be the answer.
Keep them in a min-heap of size k.
Push each value; if the heap grows past k pop the smallest; report the top once i >= k.
invariants: the heap holds exactly the min(i, k) largest values of the prefix
chooseWhen: Values stream in and k is small relative to n
tradeoffs: A Fenwick tree over values also works because arr is a permutation, at O(n log n)
hack2hire:6a04f7473141bbc31efdd6f1.variantLabel: Inferred: k-th greatest of each growing prefix

clarifyingQuestions: Can two students with the same skill both be on the team?
Is the answer the number of students or of distinct levels?
hints: Only the multiset of skills matters.
A team is a maximal run of consecutive levels.
Start runs only at levels whose predecessor is missing so each level is walked once.
invariants: each level is visited by exactly one upward walk
chooseWhen: Values are large and sparse so counting sort is impossible
tradeoffs: Sorting is simpler and O(n log n); hashing is linear but has larger constants
hack2hire:6a73bf2fd713d873ca7a77c6.variantLabel: Inferred: largest gap-free skill range, duplicates counted

constraints: 2 <= n <= 1e5 clubs; target league has 2..1e4 clubs
clarifyingQuestions: What is the earnings formula for a match?
Does each pair meet home and away?
How should the average be rounded and formatted?
hints: Write the total as a double sum over home and away clubs.
Swap the order of summation: each home club meets every other club once.
Sum the away trophies with the league total S minus the home club own count.
invariants: total and match count stay exact integers below 2**53
chooseWhen: The league is large and only aggregates are needed
tradeoffs: The closed form hides the per-match structure; the double loop is easier to audit

constraints: deletedIds are distinct non-root ids of the tree
clarifyingQuestions: Are deleted ids guaranteed to exist and exclude the root?
Is height counted in nodes or edges?
hints: Promotion never changes which kept nodes are ancestors of which.
The depth of a kept node is the number of kept nodes on its root path.
Carry that count down an explicit stack and take the maximum.
invariants: the stack entry for a node holds the number of kept nodes from the root to it, inclusive
chooseWhen: Only the resulting height is needed, not the rebuilt tree
tradeoffs: Rebuilding the tree is easier to visualise but allocates a second tree
hack2hire:69bc554c1cbff60a929be332.variantLabel: Inferred: height after deleting given nodes

clarifyingQuestions: Can the root be deleted?
Is the limit inclusive?
hints: Think about which nodes you keep: below the root, no chain of kept nodes may exceed maxHeight-1.
Group nodes by subtree height (leaves are 1); each group is an antichain.
Keeping all nodes of height below maxHeight is optimal, so delete the non-root nodes of height at least maxHeight.
invariants: subtree height of a parent exceeds every child height
chooseWhen: Deletions are unrestricted and only the count matters
tradeoffs: The layer argument needs a proof (long-path chain decomposition); a DP over depth budgets is slower but more obviously correct
hack2hire:69bc55661cbff60a929be333.variantLabel: Inferred: fewest deletions to meet a height limit

clarifyingQuestions: What happens outside the range of x?
How should non-integer results be represented?
Are queries integers?
hints: Only the highest and lowest y per distinct x matter.
Sort the distinct x values and binary search each query.
Keep the result as an exact fraction: numerator y1*(x2-x1)+(y2-y1)*(q-x1) over x2-x1, reduced by gcd.
invariants: the function is right-continuous at duplicate x using the highest y and approaches it from the left at the lowest y
chooseWhen: Many queries over a fixed point set
tradeoffs: Exact fractions avoid floating-point disagreement between languages at the cost of a string format
hack2hire:69bef92321f6ab4226963c6b.variantLabel: Inferred: piecewise linear lookup with duplicate x

clarifyingQuestions: How should fractional y be represented?
What if a gap is smaller than interval but not divisible?
hints: Each gap is handled independently.
Inserted x values step by interval from x1.
Compute y exactly as y1 + (y2-y1)*(x-x1)/(x2-x1) and reduce the fraction.
invariants: output x values are strictly increasing
chooseWhen: Time series resampling with exact values
tradeoffs: Fraction strings are exact but heavier than floats
hack2hire:696c36906b040fa4d120bc68.variantLabel: Inferred: fill gaps on a regular x grid

clarifyingQuestions: Is "descending" strict or non-increasing?
Which t if several work?
What if none works?
hints: A non-increasing array read cyclically has at most one ascent, at the wrap point.
Count the cyclic ascents.
With exactly one ascent at i, the sequence must start at i+1, which fixes t.
invariants: an all-equal array has zero cyclic ascents and every t works
chooseWhen: n is large and only one rotation can work
tradeoffs: The brute force is simpler but quadratic
hack2hire:6a19022ac81f779dc6a231ab.variantLabel: Inferred: rotation that makes the array non-increasing

clarifyingQuestions: Must every tile be used?
Is a 0 side allowed as the answer?
hints: An s x s square fits at most floor(s/2)^2 two-by-two tiles.
Use as many large tiles as fit; the rest must be one-by-one.
Feasibility is not monotone in s overall but is within even and within odd sides: binary search each.
invariants: side*side stays below 2**53 (at most about 5e9)
chooseWhen: Huge tile counts where scanning sides is too slow
tradeoffs: A direct scan is O(sqrt(M+N)) and easier to trust

clarifyingQuestions: What if there is only one leaf?
Can the path use the same leaf twice?
Is the root a leaf when it has one child?
hints: Every leaf-to-leaf path has a highest node with both children on the path.
For each node compute the best sum of a downward path ending at a leaf.
At nodes with two children combine left best + right best + value.
invariants: down[v] is the best sum of a path from v down to a leaf in its subtree
chooseWhen: Deep trees where recursion would overflow
tradeoffs: Recursion is shorter but depth reaches 1e5

clarifyingQuestions: What exactly is the score of an assignment?
Are the servers distinguishable?
Is the goal to maximise or minimise?
hints: Each absolute term is at most max - min.
Putting the global maximum in A lets A absorb every other module, leaving B and C free to be singletons; symmetrically the global minimum in C.
Compare the two resulting values using only the two smallest and two largest difficulties.
invariants: only the extreme order statistics matter
chooseWhen: n is large; only extremes are needed
tradeoffs: The closed form relies on a case argument; brute force over assignments is the independent check
hack2hire:6a949604cddc54478ddf5f33.variantLabel: Inferred: maximise a three-server partition value

constraints: 0 <= start < end <= start + 3 days, start <= 1e12 ms
clarifyingQuestions: Which time zone defines a day?
Does a call that ends exactly at midnight touch the next day?
What output shape is expected?
hints: Concurrency only rises at call starts.
Sweep per customer with ends processed before starts at the same instant.
Between events the count is constant; credit it to every day the segment touches.
invariants: the running count equals the number of calls with start <= t < end
tradeoffs: A per-day rescan is simpler but quadratic
hack2hire:696336dcf731aa3969ef52a7.variantLabel: Inferred: daily peak concurrency per customer

clarifyingQuestions: How is stability defined?
Is the answer taken modulo a prime?
Must the subset be non-empty?
hints: Fix the server with the minimum availability in the chosen set.
Given that minimum, take every server with at least that availability: reliabilities are non-negative.
Sort by availability descending and sweep with a running sum.
invariants: the running sum covers exactly the servers whose availability is at least the current one
tradeoffs: Products reach 1e15, still exact in a double; larger bounds would need BigInt
hack2hire:67a574f4b571d6ff0a4bd23a.variantLabel: Inferred: maximise min availability times total reliability
